When writing mathematical or technical content in Quarto,
use theorem environments to demarcate and highlight the structure of your content.
These environments provide consistent formatting,
automatic numbering,
and cross-reference capabilities.

Quarto provides built-in theorem environments including:

- `#thm-` for theorems
- `#lem-` for lemmas
- `#cor-` for corollaries
- `#prp-` for propositions
- `#cnj-` for conjectures
- `#def-` for definitions
- `#exm-` for examples
- `#exr-` for exercises
- `#sol-` for solutions, named after their exercise (`#exr-foo` and `#sol-foo`)
- `#rem-` for remarks

Choose the type of a result by the role the result plays,
following the standard usage of the four names [@wikipedia_theorem]:

- `#thm-`, a theorem: a central result of the page,
  one that the reader should remember and that later results build on.
- `#prp-`, a proposition: a result worth stating for its own sake,
  but smaller or more elementary than a theorem.
- `#lem-`, a lemma: a result stated mainly as a step in the proof of another result.
  A general fact extracted from a proof,
  as the section [Build every unit from smaller atomic units](teaching.qmd#build-every-unit-from-smaller-atomic-units) asks,
  is a lemma while proofs are its only use,
  and becomes a proposition once readers need it for its own sake.
- `#cor-`, a corollary: a result that follows directly from one earlier result,
  with little or no further proof,
  such as a special case of that result.
  Name that earlier result in the corollary's statement or its proof.

When more than one name fits,
test the names in the order corollary, lemma, theorem, proposition,
and use the first one that fits.
For example, on a page about [logistic regression](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html#def-logistic-regression),
the symmetry of the [logistic function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-logistic-function),
$\sigmoidf{-\logodds} = 1 - \sigmoidf{\logodds}$,
is a proposition.
The identity is elementary,
but readers need it for its own sake,
because it shows that the model treats the two classes alike.
State each result once, with one type,
and link to that div instead of restating the result under another type.

See the [Quarto documentation on theorems and proofs](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/cross-references.html#theorems-and-proofs) for complete details.

**Example syntax:**

```markdown
::: {#thm-pythagorean}

## Pythagorean theorem

In a right triangle,
the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides:

$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2.$$

:::
```

This produces automatically numbered output like "Theorem 2.1 (Pythagorean theorem)"
and can be referenced elsewhere in your document using `@thm-pythagorean`.
